result.summary: This residential intersection lacks fundamental pedestrian infrastructure, including marked crosswalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps. The roadway surface is uneven with significant patching, and there are no visible traffic control signs to regulate vehicle flow at the crossing point.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted markings to indicate a pedestrian crossing area at the intersection.

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The absence of curb ramps creates a significant barrier for individuals with mobility aids or strollers.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Uneven and patched asphalt in the intersection creates potential trip hazards for pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra-style pavement markings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Construct concrete curb ramps with detectable warning surfaces at all intersection corners.

interventions.title: Intersection Control
interventions.description: Install stop signs or other traffic calming measures to manage vehicle speeds and right-of-way.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow residential one-way street with sidewalks but a complete lack of crossing infrastructure at the intersection. There are no marked crosswalks, curb ramps, or traffic control signs visible, and parked cars obstruct sightlines at the corner.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crosswalk
hazards.description: There is no designated or marked area for pedestrians to cross the street at the intersection.

hazards.name: Missing curb ramps
hazards.description: The lack of sloped curb transitions makes the crossing inaccessible for people with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the sidewalk in the foreground

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the corner block sightlines between pedestrians waiting to cross and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street near the corner

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: ADA Compliant Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install tactile, sloped curb ramps at the corner to ensure accessibility.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the corner to improve visibility for all road users.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow residential street with sidewalks on both sides but no marked pedestrian crossings or traffic control devices. Parked vehicles along both curbs create significant visual obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross the roadway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Continuous parking on both sides of the street limits sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible street.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: No designated or marked areas for pedestrians to cross the street safely.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near intersections or mid-block crossing points to improve visibility.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at crossing points to shorten crossing distance and improve sightlines.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility crosswalk markings to designate pedestrian right-of-way.
